title: The Plonk
logline: Every few breaths, the stream goes 'plonk'. Nobody knows why. The hunt for the sound's source upstream ends in a hollow log that drips like a drum — the world's own instrument.
starting_goal: Find what makes the stream's new sound
friction_source: An unexplained sound that stops whenever they get close
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — Pip wants the map to explain it; Nimbus wants to be the one who finds it
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: listening posts -> triangulation with pebble markers -> a silent ambush that reveals the plonk needs nobody watching to happen
emotional_beat: The log becomes the garden's instrument; on still evenings they tap it gently, and the stream plonks back
rewatch_detail: The plonk's interval is constant across the whole episode — countably checkable by a rewatching child
distinctness_note: A mystery whose answer is ordinary physics; the discovery becomes an instrument, not a solution

title: The Pencil Grid
logline: Pip loses his map pencil — the good one. He divides the garden into a search grid. The pencil is found by following the snail's silver trail, which ignores the grid entirely.
starting_goal: Find the lost pencil
friction_source: A systematic search versus an un-systematic world
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — losing the tool of his trade is a small identity crack
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: grid squares -> quadrants -> a 'pencil last seen' timeline that contradicts itself while the snail slowly draws the answer behind him
emotional_beat: The grid is retired mid-search; the pencil is returned by a snail; the map gains a note: 'sometimes follow the trail, not the grid'
rewatch_detail: The pencil is visible inside the leaf pile in three earlier scenes before anyone finds it
distinctness_note: The search system fails and the living clue succeeds; humility for the method, not mockery

title: The Coolest Spot Census
logline: Hot afternoon. Which spot is coolest: under the tree, by the stream, behind the stone? The pair tests each properly. Nimbus is tempted to just BE the shade — but then nobody learns anything.
starting_goal: Find the coolest spot for the afternoon rest
friction_source: Several candidate spots and only honest testing can rank them
character_want: Nimbus: needed — being the answer by body would end the game and prove nothing; restraint is the cost
power_usage: Nimbus's body-shade is the temptation to cheat; he withholds it until the census is done, then shades everyone
escalation: Escalation by kind: hand-testing -> leaf-thermometer (which leaf wilts last) -> an official Coolness Certificate that the stream spot wins by a nose
emotional_beat: The certificate is pinned by the stream; Nimbus's shade covers the losing spots anyway — after the data is in
rewatch_detail: The wilting leaves are the episode's real scoreboard, updated scene by scene
distinctness_note: The power is the confound the experiment must exclude; science integrity at age four

title: The Quietest Place
logline: Nimbus needs a nap; everywhere has a sound. The search for absolute quiet reveals the world is never silent — and that the right hum is better than none.
starting_goal: Find a quiet place for Nimbus's nap
friction_source: The requirement is absolute; the world is relative
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — his naps are sacred to him; Pip: competent-wanted — engineering silence is a challenge he can't resist
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: quiet scale in leaf-rustle units -> hush signs for the world -> measuring the cave (too echoey), the reeds (too froggy), the hill's lee (one bee, tolerable)
emotional_beat: Nimbus falls asleep to the bee; the quiet scale is relabeled 'hum menu'; the bee gets a thank-you leaf
rewatch_detail: Each location's sound is established in earlier episodes' backgrounds — the world's audio continuity rewards rewatching
distinctness_note: A search whose answer changes the question; sensory-world comedy with zero dialogue

title: The Kite in the Tree
logline: The kite is stuck high. Nimbus can float up and fetch it — the one time flying is exactly the right tool. His worry-drip about heights wets the kite on the way down.
starting_goal: Retrieve the kite from the tree
friction_source: The retrieval is easy; the retriever's fear of his own height is not
character_want: Nimbus: needed — the job only he can do is the job that scares him
power_usage: Flight is locomotion, always available; the worry-drip (feelings leak) complicates an otherwise clean rescue
escalation: Escalation by kind: looking up (wobble) -> rising in small hops with Pip's rope-pace counts -> the grab, the drip, the damp descent, the kite needing drying anyway
emotional_beat: The kite dries on the line while Nimbus admits the height was scary; Pip admits the ground was scary too, watching; both are true
rewatch_detail: Nimbus's drip-rate visibly slows as his confidence grows across the climb — the emotional chart is on screen
distinctness_note: A fear/courage story inside a retrieval errand; the power-user is the frightened party, not the rescuer-from-above cliché inverted

title: The Lucky Pebble
logline: Pip's lucky pebble vanishes the morning of the bridge's official inspection. The search is desperate, thorough, and finally honest: the bridge was never lucky, it was level.
starting_goal: Find the lucky pebble before the inspection
friction_source: A ritual object carrying confidence it never contained
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — without the pebble he must face that the work was always his
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: retracing steps -> recruiting the snail's route data -> nominating substitute lucky pebbles that all fail audition
emotional_beat: The inspection passes pebbleless; the pebble turns up in the 'uncategorizable' cairn, where Pip decides it had retired
rewatch_detail: The pebble is visible in the cairn from scene one; the search was unnecessary the whole time
distinctness_note: Confidence located in the self, not the object; the loss is never reversed and doesn't need to be

title: The Dry Day
logline: Nimbus wakes up and cannot rain. Not sick, not sad — empty. A cloud with no rain must learn what he is on the day his one trick is gone.
starting_goal: Get through a day in which Nimbus's rain will not come
friction_source: Identity: 'if I cannot rain, am I still me?' (capacity cycle, not malfunction)
character_want: Nimbus: needed — the fear is that his whole welcome in the world is water
causal_detail: Power capacity cycle: even a mild rain has to come from somewhere; rest and absorption refill it — a bound on the power set proposed for owner review
power_usage: The premise is the power's ABSENCE; the one attempted rain produces a single apologetic drop
escalation: Escalation by kind: forcing it (one drop) -> pretending everything is normal while everyone gently works around him -> admitting emptiness to Pip, who lists everything Nimbus is that is not rain
emotional_beat: The rain returns at dusk, unforced, while he is laughing at something else; he doesn't notice until the garden does
rewatch_detail: His body is visibly less puffy all day, refilling scene by scene — the capacity gauge is drawn, not said
distinctness_note: The power bound (cost/cycle) becomes an identity story; strongest test that mild rain can carry stakes by NOT happening

title: The Key in the Stream
logline: The stream delivers a small brass key. Which lock? The pair tests every lock they know by note and errand. The answer is the muffin stall's flour chest; the reward is baked.
starting_goal: Find the lock that the found key opens
friction_source: An object whose meaning is elsewhere; ownership must be traced, not assumed
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — solving the trace is the day's detective game
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: trying known locks -> a lock census of the whole village layer -> posting a 'found: key' drawing that gets an answering drawing of a chest
emotional_beat: The stall's reply note says the chest was stuck shut for a week; inside was the good flour; tomorrow's muffins are the thank-you
rewatch_detail: The key is visible in the streambed during the previous episode's boat scene — planted, not convenient
distinctness_note: Found-object ethics (trace the owner) driving a world-mapping adventure; the reward is relationship, not treasure

title: The Unmapped Bend
logline: Pip's map ends at the reed bend. Finishing the map means going around it. Nimbus scouts from above, but from the air everything looks flat and easy — which it isn't.
starting_goal: Map the last unmapped bend of the stream
friction_source: Aerial view misleads; ground truth disagrees with the sky's report
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — a finished map is his masterpiece; Nimbus: needed — scouting is his special contribution
power_usage: Hover-scouting is locomotion; the story turns on what the aerial view CANNOT see
escalation: Escalation by kind: air report (wrong) -> ground check (mud) -> a two-layer map: sky layer in light pencil, ground truth in dark
emotional_beat: The finished map carries both views and one honest label: 'here be reeds (deeper than they look)'
rewatch_detail: The map's two-layer style returns in every later episode's background map
distinctness_note: Exploration as epistemology: two true views that must be combined; the cloud's advantage is real and insufficient

title: The Far Side of the Hill
logline: Nobody goes around the hill's far side — it's just 'the far side'. One expedition later: it's sunnier, steeper, and has its own smaller echo. The far side becomes the picnic annex.
starting_goal: Explore the hill's unvisited far side
friction_source: The unexplored is unexplored only by habit, not by danger
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — discovery is a gift he can give Pip; Pip: competent-wanted — somewhere unmapped is a small personal itch
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: formal expedition voice -> over-packed supplies -> the summit reveal that the 'far side' was visible from their own window all along
emotional_beat: They plant one flag — a ribbon — and agree the far side stays slightly wild on purpose
rewatch_detail: The far side is in the background of dozens of earlier shots; the reveal re-reads the whole world
distinctness_note: Exploration of somewhere safe that habit made invisible; wonder without peril

title: The Pebble Trail That Blew Away
logline: Into the reed maze with a pebble trail behind them. The world's mild breeze scatters the pebbles. The way home is found by ear: the stream's voice, followed.
starting_goal: Explore the reed maze and return before lunch
friction_source: A navigation system (pebble trail) destroyed by ordinary nature
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — his trail system failing in public stings; Nimbus: needed — his ears and height must replace the plan
power_usage: None; Nimbus hovers for a view but the maze defeats height too — reeds are tall
escalation: Escalation by kind: pebble trail -> string trail (snags) -> standing still and listening, the least heroic and only correct move
emotional_beat: They emerge late for lunch, unpanicked, and mark the maze entrance with a sign: 'listen for the water'
rewatch_detail: The stream's volume is directionally louder on the correct path in every maze scene — checkable by rewatchers
distinctness_note: Navigation by sensory observation after the system fails; the world is the guide, not the hazard

title: Escorting a Seed
logline: A floating seed passes by. Where will it land? The pair follows it like an escort; Nimbus gives it one gentle nudge over the stony patch — the smallest possible use of wind, on purpose, for someone else.
starting_goal: Follow one drifting seed to its landing place
friction_source: Curiosity and care versus non-interference
character_want: Nimbus: needed — one seed is helpable at exactly his scale; Pip: competent-wanted — the landing must be recorded correctly
power_usage: One micro-gust to clear stones; the debate about whether to nudge IS the story
escalation: Escalation by kind: following -> betting on the landing spot -> the nudge dilemma resolved by the smallest puff in series history
emotional_beat: The seed lands in the crack by the path; they mark it; next season's shoot gets a name in the map margin
rewatch_detail: The seed's crack is visible in earlier path scenes — the landing was set up before it happened
distinctness_note: Minimal power use as a moral choice; intervention debated rather than automatic

title: The Shadow Clock That Clouded
logline: Pip builds a sundial from a stick and stones. It works beautifully until the world's own cloud parks overhead. The day's lesson arrives instead: measure what the day actually offers.
starting_goal: Build a working shadow clock
friction_source: The instrument is right; the sky declines to cooperate
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — a working instrument is proof the world is legible; Nimbus: oddly implicated — the blocking cloud is 'family', awkwardly
power_usage: None — and Nimbus pointedly cannot move the other cloud (weather is not his to command)
escalation: Escalation by kind: recalibration -> waiting positions -> building the rain gauge instead, because the day is a rain day
emotional_beat: The sundial keeps its place for sunny days; the rain gauge gets its own stone; both instruments are 'right', weather permitting
rewatch_detail: The blocking cloud drifts off exactly when they stop watching it — a joke about attention itself
distinctness_note: Explicitly separates Nimbus from the world's weather; science adapts to conditions instead of commanding them

title: Snail Speed, Officially
logline: How fast IS the snail? Leaf-markers and counting rhymes make it official. Nimbus's excited breath-gusts keep sliding the markers — measurement versus enthusiasm.
starting_goal: Measure the snail's speed properly
friction_source: The observer's feelings disturb the experiment
character_want: Nimbus: needed — cheering the snail on matters more to him than the data; Pip: the data
power_usage: Breath-gusts slide the light markers; the interference is the leak, not a power deployment
escalation: Escalation by kind: markers slide -> heavier markers (the snail climbs over them, ruining the line) -> the solution: move the OBSERVER, not the experiment
emotional_beat: The official record is set: one leaf per count-of-ten; the certificate is presented to the snail, who begins to eat it
rewatch_detail: The marker line's drift matches Nimbus's swelling excitement in the same frames
distinctness_note: Observer effect played for comedy at preschool scale; the fix respects both science and enthusiasm

title: The Flower That Wouldn't Open
logline: Tracking which flowers open when, one flower never does. The cause is not the flower: Nimbus has been shading it every visit. Observation includes noticing yourself.
starting_goal: Learn the garden flowers' opening times
friction_source: An unobserved observer-effect: the observer is the weather
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — the flower diary is their joint science project
power_usage: Body-shade (position, not power) suppresses the flower; the reveal is behavioral
escalation: Escalation by kind: more visits -> a stake-out -> Pip's time-lapse of drawings that catches a familiar round shadow holding still over the petals
emotional_beat: Nimbus apologizes to the flower and watches from the fence; it opens mid-morning, on record, for both of them
rewatch_detail: The round shadow is present in every earlier visit scene — the evidence was always on screen
distinctness_note: The confound is the character's affection; self-awareness as the scientific method's final step

title: How Fast Is the Stream
logline: Leaf-floats and counting rhymes turn into a serious instrument: Pip calibrates the rhyme against shadow movement. The stream's speed finally has a number — until the rain upstream changes it.
starting_goal: Measure the stream's speed
friction_source: Measurement meets a world that re-rates itself mid-experiment
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — a calibrated rhyme is a crown jewel; Nimbus: needed — timing the floats is a job with rhythm
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: one float -> paired floats -> the rhyme officialized, then invalidated by upstream rain, requiring an asterisk and a second rhyme
emotional_beat: The map gains two rhymes: 'fast day' and 'slow day'; the asterisk bothers Pip until Nimbus frames it as the stream having moods too
rewatch_detail: The upstream rain is visible as a distant grey smudge two scenes before it matters
distinctness_note: Measurement under changing conditions; the world's moods prefigure the friendship's terms

title: Birdwatching Requires Stillness
logline: A finch visits the garden at dawn. Watching it requires stillness — the one thing Nimbus's excitement keeps breaking, in gusts. Self-control for love of a bird.
starting_goal: Watch the dawn finch without scaring it
friction_source: Excitement physically broadcasts; the subject is frightenable
character_want: Nimbus: needed — the finch's trust is the only medal he wants this week
power_usage: Excitement-gusts startle the finch repeatedly; stillness must be learned inside a body that leaks
escalation: Escalation by kind: hiding (gusts through the hide) -> holding his breath (wobble) -> watching from far away with the leaf-scope, laughing silently into his own fog
emotional_beat: On the third dawn the finch lands on the fence while he watches from afar; later it lands nearer — distance was the invitation
rewatch_detail: The finch's landing distance shrinks measurably across the three dawns
distinctness_note: Love expressed as restraint; the expressive power is the obstacle to overcome, not the tool

title: How Many Pebbles Sink a Leaf
logline: Cargo science: how many pebbles before the leaf-boat founders? Predictions are made, tokens placed, and Nimbus's enthusiasm loads the leaf past its prediction — twice.
starting_goal: Find the leaf-boat's cargo limit
friction_source: Prediction versus enthusiasm, at the waterline
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — a right prediction is his favorite sound; Nimbus: needed — loading is the job he gave himself
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: pebble by pebble -> double-check bets -> the ceremonial overload where both predict wrong and the snail rides the last dry leaf
emotional_beat: The limit (seven) goes on the boathouse wall; the twice-wrong predictions go up beside it, unerased
rewatch_detail: Both predictions are written large in the first scene; the result is checkable against them all episode
distinctness_note: Both leads are wrong and the record keeps the wrongness; error as decoration of the workspace

title: Don't Help the Experiment
logline: Two wet leaves: one in sun, one in shade — which dries first? Nimbus is dying to add a drop to the slow one. Science integrity versus a helper's heart.
starting_goal: Run a fair drying test between sun and shade
friction_source: Helping the losing side would spoil the knowing
character_want: Nimbus: needed — NOT helping is the hardest help he has ever not given
power_usage: The temptation is a drip; the story is about withholding it; any water drop works, his is the confessional kind
escalation: Escalation by kind: hovering over the shade leaf (shade doubles) -> fanning his hands (wind!) -> sitting on his own cloud-edge like sitting on hands
emotional_beat: Sun wins, as suspected; the result is celebrated; THEN the shade leaf gets its extra drop, with permission, after the data is safe
rewatch_detail: The shade leaf's drip-line inches across the stone all episode — a second, secret clock
distinctness_note: Premise about the ethics of experiment at age four; kindness sequenced after rigor, not instead of it

title: The Message in the Boat
logline: Where does the stream go after the bend? A boat with a leaf-sail and a drawn message is sent to find out. Days later, the board carries an answer from downstream.
starting_goal: Learn where the stream goes by sending a message-boat
friction_source: The answer can only arrive by patience and by strangers
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — the question is theirs; the answer must come from beyond their world
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: boat launched -> daily checks -> near-mutiny of impatience -> the reply drawing arrives showing a bigger stream, a bridge, and a waving stick figure
emotional_beat: The map gains its first off-map page; the downstream friend becomes a permanent pen-pal of the board
rewatch_detail: The boat is visible drifting in the far background of the next three days' scenes
distinctness_note: Science by correspondence; the implied community answers physically, enlarging the world without adding cast

title: The Controlled Gust
logline: Which dries towels faster: wind or sun? Nimbus is the wind in the experiment — which means holding one steady feeling for a whole afternoon. Science requires sincerity's opposite: consistency.
starting_goal: Run a fair wind-versus-sun drying test
friction_source: The instrument is a person; feelings fluctuate; data suffers
character_want: Nimbus: needed — being the instrument is the most useful he has ever been; steadiness is the price
power_usage: Deliberate calibrated mild wind sustained on purpose; the difficulty of sincerity-free consistency is the engine
escalation: Escalation by kind: steady gust -> a hiccup mid-test (data void, towel flaps free) -> a metronome ritual and Pip's flat jokes to keep the wind emotionally level
emotional_beat: The result: sun wins warm, wind wins fast, and the pair's towel fort uses both; the method chart survives on the boathouse wall
rewatch_detail: The hiccup is foreshadowed by Nimbus suppressing a giggle two scenes earlier
distinctness_note: The power as laboratory instrument; expression must be managed rather than leaked — the inverse episode of PN-3026's forced-rain problem

title: One Cloud Among Many
logline: Hide-and-seek, sky edition: Nimbus hides among the real clouds. Pip must find which cloud is his friend. The tell: only one cloud rains a little when it giggles.
starting_goal: Pip must find Nimbus among the sky's clouds
friction_source: Perfect camouflage defeated by an unhideable inner state
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — being found is the point of hiding; being findable is the condition of the game
power_usage: The giggle-drizzle is the giveaway; the entire game exists because the body cannot lie
escalation: Escalation by kind: still cloud (boring, safe) -> drifting disguise -> Pip's trick: tell a joke to the sky and watch which cloud leaks
emotional_beat: Found, Nimbus demands a rematch; Pip spends it teaching him to hold the giggle — the next round lasts longer, and the leak, when it comes, is triumphant
rewatch_detail: The decoy clouds are each shaped like objects from earlier episodes; the sky is a rerun gallery
distinctness_note: The signature hide-and-seek: identity located by involuntary expression; the property's thesis as a playground game

title: The Drip Trail Confession
logline: Nimbus hides Pip's surprise muffin. Hiding a secret makes him leak, and the leak makes a trail of tiny drips straight to the hiding place. The treasure map is the teller of the secret.
starting_goal: Keep the surprise muffin hidden until snack time
friction_source: Concealment produces the evidence of concealment
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — delivering the surprise cleanly would make him the author of joy
power_usage: Excited drips physically trail to the hiding spot; the reveal mechanism is the leak itself
escalation: Escalation by kind: hiding spot one (dripped on) -> spot two (drip-trail) -> Pip follows the trail kindly, slowly, pretending not to, letting the surprise survive technically
emotional_beat: The drip trail is repurposed as the official treasure-map tradition: now every surprise gets a trail on purpose
rewatch_detail: The trail's drops are countable and lead correctly — a verifiable puzzle for rewatchers
distinctness_note: The leak as narrator; Pip's merciful pretense models tact — a social skill made visible

title: The Official Hiding-Spot Map
logline: Pip maps and ranks every hiding spot in the garden. Hide-and-seek becomes solvable. The game must be saved from its own optimization.
starting_goal: Catalog the garden's hiding places
friction_source: Knowledge of the system destroys the game the system serves
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the complete map is irresistible; losing the game to it is unbearable
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: spot list -> ranking -> a points system -> both players bored to tears by fairness -> the map hidden inside the best spot, which is then banned
emotional_beat: They invent 'mapless Mondays'; the map itself becomes the sought object of a new game: hide the map
rewatch_detail: The banned best spot is never shown inside — even the audience only sees its entrance
distinctness_note: Optimization as the antagonist; choosing ignorance to preserve play — a design-philosophy episode

title: The Worry Under the Stillness
logline: Nimbus is too still. Pip knows the signs: a held-in worry. Getting it out requires not asking directly — a tea, a blanket fort, and a door left open for the truth.
starting_goal: Pip wants to help Nimbus say whatever he is not saying
friction_source: The worry is real but uninvited; extracting it by force would break it
character_want: Nimbus: not a burden — the worry is about the festival and feeling replaceable; Pip: needed as reader, not fixer
power_usage: The suppressed worry fogs Nimbus's edges progressively; the audience reads him before Pip does
escalation: Escalation by kind: casual approaches (deflected) -> the blanket fort with two mugs -> the fog thickening until it is simply named: 'you seem far away'
emotional_beat: The worry, spoken, turns out to be small and fixable; the fog lifts mid-sentence; the fort stays up two extra days by request
rewatch_detail: The fog level is a continuous hidden gauge across the episode — rewatchers can chart it
distinctness_note: Emotional detection as plot; care modeled as invitation rather than extraction

title: The Frost They Couldn't Fix
logline: First frost silvers the garden. Nimbus cannot warm anything — he has no warm. The seedlings need covers, not weather. The power's limit is the episode's spine.
starting_goal: Protect the seedlings from the first frost
friction_source: An environmental threat outside the power set entirely
character_want: Nimbus: needed — facing a weather problem he cannot weather; Pip: competent-wanted — covers and timing are craft, not magic
power_usage: Explicitly none: rain would worsen frost; the power is correctly withheld — the point of the episode
escalation: Escalation by kind: leaf blankets -> cloche jars -> a night watch with readings of the seedling thermometer-strip drawn in mud
emotional_beat: One seedling is lost anyway, honestly and gently; the row survives; a marker pebble remembers the one
rewatch_detail: The frost line's retreat is timed against the sun's shadow — two clocks crossing
distinctness_note: The strongest anti-power premise: nature exceeds the power set, craft and care fill the gap, loss is allowed to be real

title: The Low-Water Week
logline: The stream drops day by day. Water must be rationed: garden first, boats beached. The village adapts; the rain, when it comes, is the world's, and the celebration is everyone's.
starting_goal: Manage the garden through a dry week
friction_source: A shared resource shrinking on a schedule nobody controls
character_want: Both: trusted — the garden is a public duty; Nimbus's one rain cannot refill a stream and must not be asked to
power_usage: Nimbus's single rain is spent on the seedling row once, deliberately, as triage — the bound visible as policy
escalation: Escalation by kind: watering rota -> boat-beaching ceremony -> the mud parade of exposed streambed treasures, then the first returning raindrop caught in a cup
emotional_beat: The boats are re-floated to a hum; the ration chart is kept pinned as 'the week we were careful'
rewatch_detail: The stream's stone markers show the waterline falling exactly one mark per scene
distinctness_note: Scarcity managed communally; the cloud is one citizen among many, not the water department

title: The Yellow Week
logline: Pollen paints everything gold. Pip sneezes in patterns; Nimbus's sneezes come out as gusts, which move the pollen, which causes sneezing. The loop runs itself out, as seasons do.
starting_goal: Survive pollen week with dignity and open windows
friction_source: A bodily loop: sneeze-gusts redistribute the irritant
character_want: Nimbus: not a burden — his sneezes being weather makes him pollen-week's main problem; Pip: competent-wanted — his mitigation charts keep failing beautifully
power_usage: Sneeze-gusts are physiology, not power use; they shape the comedy loop without deploying the power set
escalation: Escalation by kind: handkerchief protocols -> the sneeze-loop chase -> napping it out under the laundry line while the world's breeze does the clearing
emotional_beat: The week ends on its own; the last sneeze is celebrated like a send-off; the charts go into the map's 'seasons' page
rewatch_detail: The pollen's gold overlay thins scene by scene — the whole episode is color-graded by the calendar
distinctness_note: A self-defeating body loop (sneeze moves irritant) as comedy engine; seasonal surrender as resolution

title: The Shortest Shade Day
logline: Midsummer: the tree's shade is at its smallest and everyone needs it — the plants, the snail, two friends. A shade rota is invented; Nimbus lends his body-shade where the rota fails.
starting_goal: Share the shrunken shade fairly through the hottest day
friction_source: A seasonal scarcity of comfort with multiple claimants
character_want: Nimbus: needed — his body is the only expandable shade; giving it all day costs him his own cool
power_usage: Body-shade is position, not power; his exhaustion from giving is the emotional stake
escalation: Escalation by kind: shade rota -> rota disputes -> Nimbus quietly covering everyone else's slots -> his visible droop discovered and the rota re-drawn to include HIM
emotional_beat: The rota's final column reads 'Nimbus rests'; the snail voluntarily gives up its slot, slowly, with ceremony
rewatch_detail: The shadow's size is measured hourly against a chalk line — the scarcity is drawn
distinctness_note: The giver included in the gift; care-economy episode where the helper must be assigned rest by others

title: Map Update Day
logline: The big wind night rearranges everything familiar: the sign spins, the boat drifts, the welcome stone rolls. Pip's secret joy: the map is WRONG, and wrong maps are work.
starting_goal: Survey and repair the world after the wind night
friction_source: The known world is suddenly a draft again
character_want: Pip: wanted — change is the only day his skill is fully alive; Nimbus: needed — he fears his own kind (wind) did this, unreasonably but truly
power_usage: None; the rearranging wind was the world's, which Nimbus must be told, twice
escalation: Escalation by kind: assessment walk -> triage list -> discovery that the new arrangement is better in two places and must be KEPT, not fixed
emotional_beat: Map Update Day becomes a requested ritual after every big wind; Nimbus's name goes on the 'not your fault' note pinned under the map
rewatch_detail: Two 'improvements' visible in the rearrangement are never reverted — permanent world changes traceable to this episode
distinctness_note: World-state change as gift to the cartographer; guilt-by-category (I am a cloud; wind is weather) gently dismantled
